meta.title: Mynah — record your API once, replay it offline
meta.description: Mynah is an open-source record-and-replay proxy for HTTP APIs: capture real responses in one recording pass, commit them as plain JSON tapes, and replay them byte-for-byte offline.

project.name: Mynah
project.oneLiner: Mynah sits in front of any HTTP API, records real responses to plain JSON tapes, and replays them byte-for-byte — on a plane, in CI, or two years from now.

hero.kicker: Open-source record & replay proxy for HTTP APIs
hero.headline: Record your API once. Work offline forever.

items.title: A tapes/ directory of real responses
items.detail: Every request your app made while recording, saved as readable JSON you can commit, diff and review.

items.title: Your app running fully offline
items.detail: Point its base URL at localhost:9090 and keep building with zero network — the same bytes production sent.

items.title: Deterministic tests and demos
items.detail: Replays never change under you, so flaky API-dependent tests and live-demo surprises stop.

items.title: Secrets scrubbed by default
items.detail: Authorization, Cookie and Set-Cookie headers are redacted before anything touches disk.

install.heading: Install
install.sub: One binary, no daemon, no account. Pick the package manager you already use.

methods.label: npm
methods.note: Installs the CLI globally. Requires Node.js 18 or newer.

methods.label: Homebrew
methods.note: macOS and Linux. Ships a self-contained binary — Node.js not required.

methods.label: curl
methods.note: Installs the standalone binary to ~/.local/bin. The script is short — read it first if you like.

quickstart.heading: Quickstart
quickstart.sub: From zero to an offline copy of your API in five steps.

steps.title: Point Mynah at your API
steps.explanation: Writes a commented mynah.toml with the upstream target, the proxy port (9090) and the tape directory.

steps.title: Start recording
steps.explanation: Starts the proxy on localhost:9090 — every request is forwarded upstream and every response is written to tapes/ as pretty-printed JSON.

steps.title: Run your app through the proxy
steps.explanation: One environment variable, zero code changes — click through the flows you care about once and they are on tape.

steps.title: Go offline
steps.explanation: Serves the recorded tapes on the same port; requests without a tape get a 501 and the closest recorded route, so you know exactly what to re-record.

steps.title: Commit the tapes
steps.command: git add tapes/ mynah.toml && git commit -m "Record shop API"
steps.explanation: Tapes are plain JSON, so every teammate and CI job now replays exactly the API you recorded.

faq.heading: Questions, answered
faq.sub: The five things people ask before their first recording.

items.question: How is this different from hand-written mocks?
items.answer: Mocks encode what you think the API returns. Tapes are what it actually returned — status codes, headers, pagination quirks and all — captured once and replayed byte-for-byte.

items.question: Do secrets end up in my tapes?
items.answer: No. Authorization, Cookie and Set-Cookie headers are replaced with placeholders before a tape is written, and you can list any other header or JSON field under [redact] in mynah.toml.

items.question: What happens when a request has no tape?
items.answer: In replay mode Mynah answers 501 with the method, the path and the closest recorded match, so you immediately know what to re-record. Pass --fallthrough to send unmatched requests to the real API instead.

items.question: Can I edit a tape by hand?
items.answer: Yes. Tapes are pretty-printed JSON, one file per request — tweak a price or an error body in your editor and the next replay serves your edit.

items.question: Does it only work with Node.js?
items.answer: No. Mynah is a plain HTTP proxy in front of your app, so anything that can change its API base URL can record and replay: Node, Python, Go, Rails, mobile emulators, even curl.

footer.blurb: Mynah is maintained in the open. Issues, tape ideas and pull requests are welcome — the whole proxy is a weekend read.
footer.finePrint: MIT licensed. No telemetry, no accounts, no cloud.
